content: Adding personality without losing professionalism: write in an approachable, natural voice rather than stiff corporate copy, but avoid overcorrecting into scripted-sounding forced humor; personality is best expressed through consistent, deliberate choices (color, typography, a recurring visual motif/illustration) rather than random novelty; personal touches (an about section, a candid photo) humanize without undermining credibility; the throughline in all sources is balance - personality should support the professional read, not compete with it or introduce friction/confusion for a recruiter scanning fast.
